content.user_title: Improve Code Reviews with a Team Playbook
content.value_statement: Code reviews can become inconsistent, slow, or unclear across teams. This skill provides checklists, comment patterns, templates, and review workflows for reliable feedback.
actual_capabilities: Defines a repeatable review process from context gathering through approval decisions.
Provides conventional comment labels for praise, questions, issues, bugs, and security feedback.
Includes general and language-specific checklists for quality, testing, security, APIs, and databases.
Supplies pull request and review feedback templates for structured team communication.
Explains review metrics, warning signs, and patterns for complex or security-critical reviews.
limitations: Does not execute tests, inspect live repositories, or verify code changes by itself.
Requires adaptation to each team's stack, risk tolerance, and review policies.
Example model names and API patterns may need updates for current provider documentation.
Does not replace expert review for regulated, safety-critical, or security-sensitive systems.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Reviews
use_cases.description: Create shared review expectations, comment labels, and approval criteria for a development team.

use_cases.title: Prepare Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Use self-review checklists and pull request templates before asking teammates for review.

use_cases.title: Improve Review Quality
use_cases.description: Apply security, testing, API, and architecture checklists during deeper code reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Small Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner reviewer needs a structured pass on a focused change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code review playbook to review this small pull request. Focus on correctness, tests, readability, and clear conventional comments.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare My Pull Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Author wants to self-review before requesting feedback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as my self-review partner using the playbook. Check my pull request description, testing notes, risk areas, and missing reviewer context.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Security Review Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Reviewer is checking sensitive backend or API changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the security review checklist from the playbook. Identify authentication, authorization, input validation, secrets, logging, and dependency concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Large Cross-File Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a broad architectural or high-risk pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the advanced review patterns to analyze this large change. Report systemic issues, cross-file impact, technical debt, security risks, and merge blockers.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks for help commenting on missing error handling in a service change.
output: issue: Missing error handling for the external service failure path.
If the service returns an error, the request may fail without a useful message.
Add explicit handling and include a test for the failure scenario.

output_examples.input: A team lead wants a shared pull request checklist for backend changes.
output: Review authentication and authorization on changed endpoints.
Confirm input validation, error responses, and logging behavior.
Verify tests cover success, failure, and boundary cases.

output_examples.input: A developer wants feedback on how to respond to a review disagreement.
output_examples.output: Acknowledge the concern, explain the tradeoff, offer evidence, and ask whether a follow-up task would resolve the remaining risk.

best_practices: Start with the pull request purpose before reviewing individual lines.
Use conventional comments to separate blockers from optional suggestions.
Keep feedback specific, actionable, and tied to user impact or maintainability.
anti_patterns: Blocking merges on personal style preferences without objective impact.
Approving large changes without checking tests, edge cases, and security risks.
Submitting pull requests without context, testing notes, or self-review.

faq.question: Can this skill review code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides review guidance and templates, but the agent still needs the code or pull request context.

faq.question: Does it support security reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes security checklists for authentication, authorization, input validation, data protection, dependencies, and logging.

faq.question: Is it only for senior engineers?
faq.answer: No. It includes beginner-friendly review steps and advanced patterns for complex changes.

faq.question: Can teams customize the comment labels?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can adapt labels, blocking rules, and templates to match local workflow.

faq.question: Does it replace CI checks?
faq.answer: No. It recommends using CI for routine checks and human review for logic, design, and risk.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
